title: Canonical finite constant adjunct characterized by coefficient one
statement: For a commutative ring A, a scheme Y and a module-sheaf map m from the constant rank-one A-module on Y to the ordinary direct image of that module on the projective line, suppose its underlying abelian map takes coefficient one to coefficient one under finiteConstantAbComparison, in the precise displayed monoid-unit equation. Then the single of m followed by the canonical single-object right-derived augmentation, and by the inverse finite unit comparison on the projective line, equals the inverse finite unit comparison on Y followed by finiteUnitAdjunct A Y. This concerns only the native finite constant sheaves; there is no condensed coefficient, realization functor, supplied right-derived model or comparison square.

source.place: paragraph (1), the finite constant coefficient unit and its canonical derived adjunct

proof.text: Under the constant-sheaf adjunction, a map from the constant rank-one A-module is determined by the image of coefficient one on terminal sections. The constant/forgetful comparison identifies that coefficient one with the displayed monoid-object unit. The hypothesis therefore identifies m with the ordinary adjunct of the canonical constant-sheaf pullback isomorphism. This uses no nonzero-ring or nonempty-scheme assumption.

Apply the canonical derived counit normalization on a single complex and the triangle identity to this ordinary adjunct. Its derived adjunct is the single of m, then the inverse single/termwise comparison, then the canonical right-derived unit on the single complex. Exactness is needed only for inverse image, not for direct image.

Expand geoP1UnitPullback and the ordinaryFiniteUnitPullback hom formula. Naturality of exact single comparisons and uniqueness of the constant-object left adjoints show that finiteUnitComparison identifies this pullback with the native constant-sheaf pullback. Transport the derived adjunct through these source and target comparisons to obtain the stated equality.

lean.statement:
theorem finite_constant_adjunct_of_one
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] (Y : Scheme.{u})
    (m : geoCartierConstant A Y ⟶
      (lowerStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) (ProjectiveLine Y ↘ Y)).obj
        (geoCartierConstant A (ProjectiveLine Y)))
    (h : (@MonObj.one _ _ _ (finiteConstantAbRing A Y)
        ((sfbConstantRing Y).obj (RingCat.of A)).mon) ≫ (finiteConstantAbComparison A Y).inv ≫
        (sheafCompose (Scheme.ProEt.topology Y)
          (forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) Ab.{u + 1})).map m ≫
        (lowerStar Ab.{u + 1} (ProjectiveLine Y ↘ Y)).map
          (finiteConstantAbComparison A (ProjectiveLine Y)).hom =
      Functor.LaxMonoidal.ε (lowerStar Ab.{u + 1} (ProjectiveLine Y ↘ Y)) ≫
        (lowerStar Ab.{u + 1} (ProjectiveLine Y ↘ Y)).map
          (@MonObj.one _ _ _ (finiteConstantAbRing A (ProjectiveLine Y))
        ((sfbConstantRing (ProjectiveLine Y)).obj (RingCat.of A)).mon)) :
    (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).map m ≫
      DerivedCategory.Q.map
        ((HomologicalComplex.singleMapHomologicalComplex
          (lowerStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) (ProjectiveLine Y ↘ Y))
          (.up ℤ) 0).inv.app (geoCartierConstant A (ProjectiveLine Y))) ≫
      (lowerStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) (ProjectiveLine Y ↘ Y)).rightDerivedFunctorUnitQ
        ((HomologicalComplex.single _ (.up ℤ) 0).obj
          (geoCartierConstant A (ProjectiveLine Y))) ≫
      (geoP1Pushforward A (ProjectiveLine Y ↘ Y)).map
        (finiteUnitComparison A (ProjectiveLine Y)).inv =
    (finiteUnitComparison A Y).inv ≫ finiteUnitAdjunct A Y
